speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and culture suggest a bacterial infection, likely secondary to your recent cold, but the lack of focal consolidation on the X-ray makes typical pneumonia less likely. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal FeNO and methane levels make an active asthma exacerbation or small airways disease less likely, despite your smoking history. speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening symptoms in cold, dry air is very characteristic of chronic bronchitis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Given your smoking history and the positive *Haemophilus influenzae* culture, we need to assess your lung volumes and airflow obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis (likely due to *Haemophilus influenzae* superinfection), with underlying airway hyperresponsiveness from past dust exposure.
